[[File:Cynthia Vinzant MFO 2017.jpg|thumb|Vinzant at the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]] in 2017]]
'''Cynthia Vinzant''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[real algebraic geometry]]; her research has also involved [[algebraic combinatorics]], [[matroid theory]], [[Hermitian matrix|Hermitian matrices]], and [[spectrahedron|spectrahedra]] in [[convex optimization]]. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Washington]].{{r|uw}}

==Education and career==
Vinzant is a 2007 graduate of [[Oberlin College]] in Ohio, where she studied mathematics and neuroscience.{{r|bio}} She completed her Ph.D. in mathematics in 2011 at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], with the dissertation ''Real Algebraic Geometry in Convex Optimization'' supervised by [[Bernd Sturmfels]].{{r|bio|mg}}

After working as a Hildebrandt Assistant Professor at the [[University of Michigan]] and as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing]] in Berkeley, Vinzant obtained a tenure-track assistant professor position at [[North Carolina State University]] in 2015. She moved to the University of Washington in 2021 and was promoted to associate professor in 2023.{{r|bio}} 

==Recognition==
In 2020, Vinzant was named as a [[Sloan Research Fellow]] in mathematics{{r|sloan}} and as a von Neumann Fellow at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].{{r|bio|ias}} She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2024 class of fellows.{{r|fams}} Vinzant and colleagues will receive<ref name="2025HeldPrize">{{cite web | title=News from the AMS - Michael and Sheila Held Prize | website=American Mathematical Society | date=3 February 2025 | url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7430 | access-date=12 February 2025}}</ref> the 2025 ''Michael and Sheila Held Prize''<ref name="a572">{{cite web | title=Michael and Sheila Held Prize – NAS | website=NAS | date=22 January 2025 | url=https://www.nasonline.org/award/michael-and-sheila-held-prize/ | access-date=12 February 2025}}</ref> from the [[National Academy of Sciences]].
